column8: Overexpress a feedback-resistant mutant (e.g., lysC^T311I) to relieve allosteric inhibition by L-lysine and L-threonine, removing the primary bottleneck at the entry of the aspartate-derived lysine pathway.

Dihydrodipicolinate synthase catalyzes the first committed step toward L-lysine/DAP; strengthening this branch-point enzyme increases carbon flux from aspartate semialdehyde toward lysine biosynthesis.

Downregulating homoserine dehydrogenase reduces drain of aspartate semialdehyde toward threonine/methionine, and lowers intracellular threonine pools, which synergistically weakens feedback inhibition on aspartate kinase.
Partial attenuation of thrB prevents threonine over-accumulation and avoids back-conversion/repressive effects on the aspartate kinase reaction, improving net lysine flux.

Overexpressing pyruvate carboxylase increases anaplerotic replenishment of oxaloacetate from pyruvate, supplying the carbon skeleton needed to support high-level lysine biosynthesis under aerobic glucose metabolism.

Reducing PEP carboxykinase activity prevents decarboxylation of oxaloacetate back to PEP during gluconeogenesis, conserving carbon and energy (ATP) and increasing oxaloacetate availability for the aspartate/lysine pathway.
